requirements.title: Execute conforming programs within qualified processor limits
requirements.source: 4.2 p2(1); J3/24-007 PDF 46, printed 32, lines 9-11; qualifications in p5-p6, PDF 46-47.
requirements.definition: The processor must execute standard-conforming programs according to the document's interpretations, subject to the size and complexity limits it may impose. This is a real universal processor obligation, not a definition of notation. It does not promise identical execution across processors or supply missing non-Fortran dependencies. Processor-dependent facilities retain their qualified methods or semantics under p6.

pending.whole-suite-execution: Finite observational aggregation is now represented by doc/evidence/whole_suite_execution.json, without another program or facet-completion credit. Still needs a content-bound independently reviewed source/requirement census, complete conforming fixture/effect-oracle inventory, and separately justified size, complexity, optional-facility and external-dependency qualifications. Current exact-ID, phase/mode/profile observations preserve failures, skips, missing members and unexecuted effects. An XFAIL, undocumented failure or generic resource explanation cannot remove a requirement from the denominator. The incomplete global source census and qualification evidence keep this facet pending; no finite run certifies the universal claim.

requirements.oracle_limitation: No executable case or completion credit is assigned to this universal facet. The finite execution ledger binds the current whole collected case set, including separately classified negative/admission/context evidence. A partial invocation cannot silently shrink that set. An aggregate's current source/inventory review is not source completeness, successful execution, or an independent effect test; the ordinary cases retain their primary R/C/S owners. Documentation is a proposed way to qualify evidence, not a conversion of p7-p8 recommendations into mandatory processor documentation.
requirements.dependencies: 4.2 p1 distinguishes program and program-unit conformance; 5.2.1-.2 (PDF 56) includes non-Fortran-defined entities and requires exactly one main program. 4.2 p5 spans PDF 46 lines 42-43 and PDF 47 lines 1-2. Paragraphs 6-8 (PDF 47 lines 3-11) preserve processor-dependent semantics and documentation modality.

requirements.title: Capability to report syntactically detectable obsolescent usage
requirements.source: 4.2 p2(2), qualified by p3; J3/24-007 PDF 46, printed 32, lines 12-14 and 33-34.
requirements.definition: The processor must have a capability to detect and report obsolescent forms in a submitted program unit insofar as numbered syntax rules and constraints make their use detectable. Obsolescent does not mean deleted or nonconforming. Paragraph 3 removes the obligation to detect or report such usage inside a format specification that is not part of a FORMAT statement. It does not forbid a processor from reporting it.

pending.obsolescent-reporting-capability: Needs a reviewed obsolescent-form census from the defining source and typography, joined to numbered detectability, FORMAT-exception status, and qualified reporting configurations for each processor/version. Collect actual located reports in those configurations, with conforming controls and exact nonfatal predicates where applicable. The existing diagnose outcome denotes invalid input, so it cannot honestly represent a conforming obsolescent program merely expected to warn. A conforming-reporting evidence contract and whole-census aggregation remain to be designed outside this unit.

requirements.oracle_limitation: No invalid-input fixture, generic warning allowance, or requirement to reject obsolescent syntax is invented. A report absent in one invocation does not by itself prove absence of the processor capability. Reading the Annex B introduction or the small-type convention does not approve every obsolescent feature.
requirements.dependencies: 4.1.5 p1 identifies smaller-type descriptions; 4.4.3 p2 (PDF 52) refers back to it. B.3.1 (PDF 577) lists obsolescent features but is not individually catalogued here. 13.2.1-.2 (PDF 289) distinguishes FORMAT statements from character-supplied format specifications.

requirements.title: Capability to report violations of numbered syntax and constraints
requirements.source: 4.2 p2(3), qualified by p3; J3/24-007 PDF 46, printed 32, lines 15-17 and 33-34; 4.1.2 p3, PDF 45 lines 7-12.
requirements.definition: The processor must have a capability to detect and report forms or relationships in a submitted program unit that the numbered syntax rules or constraints do not permit, including deleted features described in Annex B. This does not require every prose restriction to be diagnosed, nor does it supersede the other explicit p2 reporting categories. For a format specification outside a FORMAT statement, p3 exempts deleted features and additional forms or relationships from required detection/reporting. The exemption does not make an invalid format conforming.

pending.syntax-reporting-capability: Needs an independently reviewed complete R inventory and actual enclosing-context witnesses, with correct grammar premises, explicit p3 classifications, qualified processor reporting modes, and input/statement-located diagnostic observations. Aggregate accepted extensions and nonfatal reports without imposing a fatal-rejection oracle. Current-run successes or failures remain finite evidence; no one malformed program establishes this universal capability.
pending.constraint-reporting-capability: Needs the equivalent source-bound C inventory, associated-term use graph and valid/isolated-invalid evidence, preserving the broad-prose versus numbered-subset distinction in 4.1.2 p3. The new C401 IF report is owned by C401 only and does not satisfy this aggregate facet. Keep additional rejection/rule-code policies distinct from the standard's report capability.
pending.deleted-feature-reporting-capability: Needs individual review of the deleted forms described in Annex B and their current numbered-grammar exclusions, including FORMAT-statement versus non-FORMAT-specification placement. Use documented reporting modes and exact attributable messages. An annex-level reference is not source closure of B.1/B.2, and an unlocated driver summary, crash or unrelated diagnostic cannot serve as a witness.

requirements.oracle_limitation: No executable case is credited here. The existing C1302 character-format negatives deliberately use oracle_basis=lfortran-policy and are not mandatory-detection evidence. The same legacy container also contains a FORMAT-statement case; its source has a standard reporting obligation, but its stronger rejection contract and shared metadata are left unchanged for parent review.
requirements.dependencies: 4.1.1 requires constraints and text in addition to the displayed BNF; 4.1.2 p2-p3 propagates associated constraints without numbering every prose restriction. 13.2.1/R1301-R1302 and 13.2.2 p1 (PDF 289), plus 13.3.1/C1302 (PDF 290), supply the exact format boundary. Annex B explicitly identifies deleted features (PDF 576-577); its individual items remain outside this catalogue.

requirements.title: Capability to report unsupported intrinsic kind values
requirements.definition: For a submitted program unit, the processor must have a capability to detect and report an intrinsic type used with a kind type parameter value that it does not support. Kind support is processor-specific and type-specific. Unsupported representation is distinct from disagreement between two supported kinds in a user-procedure call.

pending.unsupported-kind-reporting-capability: Needs a qualified, versioned support inventory for each intrinsic type and a justified unsupported value, plus a minimally repaired supported-kind control and a located reporting observation in a documented capability mode. Do not assume that kind numbers denote byte counts, that a large arbitrary number is unsupported, or that 4/8/1/4 kinds exist universally. Aggregate the type-specific evidence; the registry cannot currently express the support-inventory documentary premise.

requirements.oracle_limitation: No guessed kind value, optional-kind skip, or dummy-argument mismatch is presented as this obligation's test. Legacy S15.5.2.4 cases address actual 15.5.2.5 p2-p3 prose and retain their independent LFortran policy basis; they are not renamed or counted here.
requirements.dependencies: 7.4.1/R704-R706/C717 (PDF 80) and 7.4.4.2/R721/C724 (PDF 84) distinguish intrinsic kinds and supported representation methods. 15.5.2.5 p1 begins on PDF 339; p2-p3 are on PDF 340 lines 1-10, not in 15.5.2.4.

requirements.title: Capability to report prohibited source form and characters
requirements.source: 4.2 p2(5); J3/24-007 PDF 46, printed 32, lines 20-21; p3, lines 33-34 where applicable.
requirements.definition: The processor must have a capability to detect and report source-form or character usage in a submitted program unit that Clause 6 does not permit. The obligation is not limited to restrictions carrying R/C numbers. Establish the selected source form, the processor's character representation and the actual prohibited context before judging a witness. Preserve the p3 exemption for additional forms or relationships inside a non-FORMAT format specification where relevant.

pending.source-form-reporting-capability: Needs source-census aggregation of Clause 6 restrictions across actual free/fixed selection mechanisms, with byte-preserved inputs when layout is material, minimal repairs, precise file/line or bounded statement spans, and versioned reporting-mode evidence. Reuse canonical Clause 6 observations without reassigning their facets. A current invocation's failure is not automatically absence of a general capability; a crash, limit failure or wrong-location report never passes.
pending.source-character-reporting-capability: Needs an independently qualified source-interface character/encoding/repertoire contract, canonical Clause 6 context review, and located reports in documented capability modes. A dollar glyph, arbitrary Unicode byte sequence, native character code assumption, unrelated warning or guessed driver-file attribution is insufficient. Do not convert unsupported mandatory behavior into a profile skip.

requirements.oracle_limitation: No new source-form/character fixtures are duplicated here. The existing diagnose contract can observe justified invalid-input reports, including tightly qualified nonfatal messages, but cannot certify source-interface documentation or whole-Clause-6 capability.
requirements.dependencies: 6.1.1 (PDF 67) partitions the processor character set; 6.1.6 (PDF 68) restricts additional-character contexts. 6.3 and 6.4 (PDF 71-74) distinguish source forms, actual statements and INCLUDE lines. Those catalogues and the separate INCLUDE work unit retain their owners.

requirements.title: Capability to report Clause 19 scope inconsistencies
requirements.definition: The processor must have a capability to detect and report name usage in a submitted program that conflicts with Clause 19 scope rules for names, labels, operators or assignment symbols. The submission scope here is a program, unlike the program-unit wording of most neighboring items. This is not a promise that every inconsistency can be discovered while compiling an isolated source file.

pending.name-scope-reporting-capability: Needs an independently reviewed Clause 19 name/scope census, complete submitted-program composition, and qualified processor checking stages/modes. Preserve global, local and nested-scope distinctions, association and inaccessible identifiers. Whole-program evidence cannot be fabricated from one separately compiled source or an unrelated link failure.
pending.label-scope-reporting-capability: Needs canonical label-scope restrictions and whole-program submission assumptions joined to isolated, located report witnesses and valid controls. Existing lexical label syntax tests are not a substitute for Clause 19 scope coverage.
pending.operator-scope-reporting-capability: Needs canonical defined/generic-operator scope and association premises, complete interfaces and program inputs, plus attributable reports in the processor's documented checking mode. A malformed operator token is not a scope witness.
pending.assignment-scope-reporting-capability: Needs canonical assignment-symbol/generic scope and association premises with valid interfaces and complete program composition, followed by located diagnostic observations. An assignment type error or missing object file does not establish the intended scope report.

requirements.oracle_limitation: All four aggregate facets remain pending. No single-source test is relabeled as proof of whole-program diagnosis, and prose scope restrictions are not excluded merely because they lack numbered constraints.
requirements.dependencies: 19.1 p2 (PDF 548 lines 4-10) distinguishes identifier scopes and nested/inaccessible exceptions; 19.2 (PDF 548 lines 23-32) introduces global identifiers. Detailed 19.3-19.5 obligations remain to be catalogued under their own owners. 5.2.2 (PDF 56) defines the complete program.

requirements.title: Capability to report nonstandard intrinsic procedures
requirements.definition: The processor must have a capability to detect and report use of a nonstandard intrinsic procedure in a submitted program unit. This explicitly includes a procedure sharing a standard intrinsic's name but having different requirements. The reporting capability remains required even when the processor permits the extension.

pending.additional-intrinsic-reporting-capabilit: Needs a qualified processor/version intrinsic-extension inventory, proof that the reference resolves intrinsically rather than to a user external, and a documented extension-reporting mode. Join actual extension uses and minimal conforming alternatives to precise reports; if no such extension exists, establish that through evidence rather than a passing dummy program or profile skip.
pending.altered-intrinsic-reporting-capability: Needs the standard intrinsic's defining requirements and a documented same-name extension that actually differs, with arguments otherwise valid and a specific extension-use report. Do not infer nonstandard requirements from a name match or from a supported standard overload.

requirements.oracle_limitation: No processor-specific intrinsic is guessed. An external procedure sharing an intrinsic spelling is not automatically a use of a nonstandard intrinsic. The p4 name-conflict permission and EXTERNAL protection must be resolved before any fixture is authored.
requirements.dependencies: 4.2 p4 (PDF 46 lines 35-41) governs permitted intrinsic additions and program restrictions. 8.5.9 (PDF 128) specifies EXTERNAL. Clause 16 retains ownership of the standard intrinsic requirements; this catalogue does not approve that inventory.

requirements.title: Capability to report nonstandard intrinsic modules
requirements.definition: The processor must have a capability to detect and report use of a nonstandard intrinsic module in a submitted program unit. A missing nonintrinsic module or arbitrary unresolved USE name is not evidence of this obligation.

pending.nonstandard-module-reporting-capability: Needs a versioned inventory showing that the processor provides the selected additional module intrinsically, standard/nonstandard ownership review, and its documented extension-reporting mode. Submit a use with no unrelated missing declarations or files and require a report identifying that use. A no-extension processor needs documentary/implementation evidence, not an invented unavailable-module negative.

requirements.oracle_limitation: No executable case is assigned without an intrinsic-module identity premise. Neither successful USE of a standard module nor failure to locate an arbitrary module establishes this capability.
requirements.dependencies: 14.2.1 p1 (PDF 317 lines 19-22) distinguishes processor-provided intrinsic modules from nonintrinsic modules. 4.2 p4 separately forbids a standard-conforming program from using a processor-added nonstandard intrinsic module.

requirements.title: Capability to report nonstandard procedures in standard intrinsic modules
requirements.definition: The processor must have a capability to detect and report, in a submitted program unit, use of a procedure from a standard intrinsic module when the procedure is absent from this document or has requirements different from those it specifies. This is separate from using a nonstandard module. A procedure being provided by an intrinsic module does not itself make that procedure intrinsic.

pending.additional-module-procedure-reporting-ca: Needs a qualified export inventory for an actual standard intrinsic module showing a processor-added procedure, source ownership review, valid call premises and a documented reporting mode. Require an attributable extension-use report rather than a missing-symbol or module-file failure.
pending.altered-module-procedure-reporting-capab: Needs the canonical module procedure's complete requirements compared with a documented extension to those requirements, a source-valid control, and a located report on the extension use. A changed interface must not be inferred merely from reference-compiler disagreement.

requirements.oracle_limitation: Both facets need non-executable module/interface evidence before meaningful execution can be designed. They are not folded into the nonstandard-intrinsic-procedure or nonstandard-module facets.
requirements.dependencies: 14.2.1 p2 (PDF 317 line 23) explicitly distinguishes procedures/types in intrinsic modules from intrinsic entities. The relevant standard module and procedure definitions in Clauses 16-18 remain separate source owners.

requirements.title: Capability to report why a submitted program is rejected
requirements.definition: The processor must have a capability to detect and report the reason for rejecting a submitted program. This does not mandate rejection of every nonconforming program, a particular error code, or fatal severity for the other reporting obligations. It concerns the reason for a rejection, not just an unsuccessful exit status.

pending.rejection-reason-reporting-capability: Needs a qualified inventory of processor rejection categories and reporting modes, paired with actual submitted-program observations that identify the corresponding reason. Distinguish language diagnostics, documented size/complexity refusals, unsupported dependencies and tool/harness failures. A generic driver failure, unlocated summary, crash, timeout, signal or exhausted resource is not a passing source-diagnostic witness. Non-source rejection reasons need a separate explicit evidence contract, not abuse of compile-only diagnose with invented input attribution.

requirements.oracle_limitation: One rejected C401 IF cannot establish all rejection-reason capability. The current invalid-input reporting contract remains file/line-bound; no runner change or success-shaped fallback is introduced for general processor reasons.
requirements.dependencies: 4.2 p2(1) preserves processor size/complexity limits and p5 preserves out-of-scope demands. Paragraph 7 recommends documenting limits and their reporting, but that recommendation is not converted here into a mandatory documentation requirement.

requirements.title: Conditions on processor extensions and external-name conflicts
requirements.source: 4.2 p4, first three sentences; J3/24-007 PDF 46, printed 32, lines 35-39.
requirements.definition: A processor may add forms and relationships only subject to compatibility with the standard ones. The explicit exception permits additional intrinsic procedures even when a procedure name in a standard-conforming program could conflict. For a collision involving an external procedure, selecting the intrinsic is permitted unless the name has the EXTERNAL attribute where it is used. That permission does not authorize overriding a name so declared EXTERNAL. These are conditional restrictions on a processor that supplies extensions, not a requirement to supply any particular extension.

pending.extension-compatibility: Needs a qualified processor extension inventory and independently reviewed compatibility analysis against the applicable standard forms and relationships, with explicit intrinsic-name exceptions. Add differential conforming execution evidence only for justified overlap contexts. No-extension applicability must be evidenced, not inferred from an unrecognized-token rejection. The non-executable inventory/compatibility contract is not representable as a current registry case.
pending.external-attribute-protection: Needs a documented additional intrinsic and a justified actual collision with a conforming external procedure, together with a complete external implementation and EXTERNAL at the use. A future finite control must prove which procedure executes without uninitialized data or unsupported kinds. Do not substitute a standard intrinsic, a guessed extension, an internal procedure or a compiler-option accident for the source premise.

requirements.oracle_limitation: No artificial extension fixture is created. Permission to select an intrinsic without EXTERNAL is not an obligation to do so. Capability to report extension use is separately retained in p2(3)/(7)-(9), even when extension acceptance is permitted.
requirements.dependencies: 8.5.9 p1 and its constraints (PDF 128) supply the EXTERNAL attribute. 4.2 p1/p4 preserve conforming-program meaning and distinguish intrinsic use from a same-named external. Detailed procedure resolution and standard intrinsic semantics stay with their defining clauses.

requirements.title: Conforming programs avoid processor-added nonstandard intrinsics and modules
requirements.source: 4.2 p4, final sentence; J3/24-007 PDF 46, printed 32, lines 40-41.
requirements.definition: A standard-conforming program cannot use a processor-added nonstandard intrinsic procedure or intrinsic module. Acceptance as an extension does not make the program standard conforming. This restriction does not prohibit an otherwise conforming user external procedure merely because it shares a spelling with an additional intrinsic; resolve the p4 name-conflict/EXTERNAL conditions first.

pending.nonstandard-procedure-use: Needs a source/interface conformance review resolving every selected intrinsic use against the pinned standard and qualified processor extension inventory. Any finite positive control proves only its actual resolved uses. An isolated extension-use diagnostic additionally needs the S4.2-007 premises and documented reporting mode; no portable fixture can simply assume a particular extra intrinsic exists.
pending.nonstandard-module-use: Needs the corresponding module-use conformance review and intrinsic/nonintrinsic ownership evidence, joined to the processor's actual provided modules. Diagnostic observations require S4.2-008 premises, not a fabricated missing-module failure. Whole-program absence of nonstandard module use is non-executable source/interface evidence.

requirements.oracle_limitation: The required diagnostic basis is explicitly p2(7)-(8), not a blanket rule that every prose shall implies a compile error. No hello-world is counted as proving that all conforming programs avoid extensions, and no module-procedure extension is silently reclassified as an intrinsic procedure.
requirements.dependencies: 4.2 p2(7)-(9) distinguishes intrinsic procedures, intrinsic modules and procedures in standard intrinsic modules. 14.2.1 p1-p2 (PDF 317) and 8.5.9 (PDF 128) provide the identity and EXTERNAL premises.

requirements.title: Provide processor-dependent facilities with processor-determined interpretation
requirements.definition: Facilities identified as processor dependent are incompletely specified by the document, but must nevertheless be provided, using methods or semantics determined by the processor. Processor dependence is not permission to omit a required facility or to invent a portable fixed outcome. Conditions and optionality in each facility's defining source still govern its applicability. The separate p8 documentation recommendation retains its should modality.

pending.processor-dependent-facility-provision: Needs an independently reviewed whole-source inventory of processor-dependent facilities, including their defining conditions and optional properties, joined to qualified processor implementation/interface evidence. Where a facility has an executable observable, collect its canonical tests separately. A failed mandatory implementation is not an unavailable optional profile and must not be silently skipped.
pending.processor-determined-methods-semantics: Needs qualified, versioned evidence establishing the processor's actual methods or semantics for each applicable facility, followed by only those executable assertions justified by that evidence. Keep unspecified/undefined results and explicitly permitted choices distinct. A runtime probe cannot silently supply both the claimed premise and its own expected result; documentation/interface review is a proposed evidence route, not an extra shall requirement.

requirements.oracle_limitation: No context-only program, placeholder zero value, general profile skip or invented processor-independent oracle is supplied. The current registry cannot express complete documentary/interface/census aggregation; both facets remain explicit pending work.
requirements.dependencies: 4.2 p2(1)/p5 qualifies execution claims; p7-p8 recommends associated documentation. Existing character-graphics, source-interface and processor-profile gaps remain separately owned and cannot be closed by this general statement.

accounting.rationale: PDF 46 lines 6-8: distinguishes the two conditions for program conformance from the embedding definition for a program unit.
Program conformance uses only the forms and relationships the document describes. This definition is not a hello-world execution requirement or permission to omit prose restrictions.
The program must also have an interpretation under the document. Merely being accepted by one processor, or satisfying the displayed BNF alone, does not establish that condition.
A program unit conforms if it can participate in a standard-conforming program. It need not be an independently executable main program. 5.2.1-.2 (PDF 56) supplies the distinct unit/program concepts.

PDF 46 lines 9-32: all ten processor obligations are preserved individually. Most reporting items concern a submitted program unit; (1), (6) and (10) concern a program. Capability and per-invocation outcomes are not equated.
PDF 46 lines 10-11: conforming execution with both size and complexity qualifications.
Execution must follow the document's interpretations; source-only definitions are not substitutes for this universal obligation.
Processor-imposed program-size limits qualify the obligation. A failure cannot be excluded merely by calling it a limit without justified processor evidence.
Program-complexity limits are a separate stated qualification and are not lost in a size-only interpretation.
PDF 46 lines 12-14: reporting capability for obsolescent usage in a submitted program unit, with the following detectability limitation and p3 exception.
The requirement extends only insofar as numbered syntax rules and constraints can detect the obsolescent form.
PDF 46 lines 15-17: both forms and relationships excluded by numbered syntax/constraints, including deleted features.
Excluded forms are included; syntax acceptance alone is not a report.
Excluded relationships are also included; lexical token errors are not the whole obligation.
Deleted features described in Annex B are expressly included, subject to p3. Their individual source accounting remains pending outside this scope.
PDF 46 lines 18-19: unsupported intrinsic kind values, with processor/type support premises.
PDF 46 lines 20-21: source form and characters prohibited by Clause 6, including prose restrictions.
Both actual source-form selection and the violated Clause 6 restriction need evidence.
Source-character identity, representability and prohibited context cannot be inferred from arbitrary bytes or graphics.
PDF 46 lines 22-23: the submission is a program, and all four listed scope-rule classes are included.
Clause 19 scope rules for names.
Clause 19 scope rules for labels, not just label token syntax.
Clause 19 scope rules for operators.
Clause 19 scope rules for assignment symbols.
PDF 46 lines 24-26: nonstandard intrinsic-procedure use, including the same-name/different-requirements case.
Additional intrinsic procedures require a processor identity and intrinsic-resolution premise.
A standard intrinsic spelling does not waive reporting when the procedure has nonstandard requirements.
PDF 46 lines 27-28: nonstandard intrinsic modules, not arbitrary unavailable nonintrinsic modules.
PDF 46 lines 29-31: two alternatives for procedures from a standard intrinsic module.
The module is standard but the procedure is absent from the document.
The procedure has requirements different from the document's definition.
PDF 46 line 32: capability to report the reason for rejecting a submitted program, not a rule that all reports must reject.

PDF 46 lines 33-34: a narrowly situated waiver of detection/reporting, with all three listed categories and both additional-form/relationship branches retained. It neither requires silence nor legalizes an invalid format.

The waiver is for a format specification not forming part of a FORMAT statement. It includes character-supplied specifications; a malformed actual FORMAT statement is not exempt. No compiler-time versus runtime distinction is substituted for this source-context distinction.
Deleted forms in that non-FORMAT specification need not be detected or reported.
Obsolescent forms in that non-FORMAT specification need not be detected or reported.
Additional forms in that non-FORMAT specification need not be detected or reported. The same missing comma in an actual FORMAT statement has a different diagnostic basis.
Additional relationships in that non-FORMAT specification are also exempt from mandatory detection/reporting; validity under 13.2.2 remains separate.
PDF 46 lines 35-41: compatible-extension condition, intrinsic-name exception, external-name/EXTERNAL qualification, and two program prohibitions are kept distinct.

Permission to add forms and relationships is conditional on not conflicting with standard forms and relationships; this genuine conditional processor restriction is not discarded as an unconditional permission.

Additional intrinsic procedures are expressly allowed even if their names could conflict with procedure names in a conforming program. This is an exception to the preceding compatibility condition, not an obligation to add such procedures.
Where the conflict involves an external-procedure name, the processor is allowed, but not required, to choose the intrinsic. The following EXTERNAL exception is essential.
The intrinsic-selection permission does not apply when the name has EXTERNAL where used. Its protection needs an actual documented extension/collision premise, not a guessed extra intrinsic.
A conforming program cannot use processor-added nonstandard intrinsic procedures.
A conforming program cannot use processor-added nonstandard intrinsic modules.
PDF 46 lines 42-43 continues on PDF 47 lines 1-2. This limits what conformance implies about execution; the complete cross-page qualification is subdivided below.
A conforming program can impose demands outside the document's scope.
Items allowed by the standard need not be portable between all processors.
External procedures defined other than by Fortran are the source's example of such nonportable standard items; their availability is not supplied by a Fortran syntax test.
Conformance alone does not ensure consistent execution on all processors or even successful execution on any processor. This qualification does not erase p2(1)'s within-premise execution obligation.
PDF 47 lines 3-4: incomplete specification is separated from the genuine obligation to provide the facilities and the processor's choice of methods or semantics.
The document intentionally does not fully specify processor-dependent semantics; that is not an undefined-result assertion or a blanket optionality rule.
The facilities still have to be provided. Missing support cannot be silently reclassified as a definition or an optional profile.
Their methods or semantics are determined by the processor. An evidence contract must qualify that interpretation instead of inventing a universal constant result.

PDF 47 lines 5-9 recommends processor documentation. This should is advisory normative text, not a mandatory shall or an informative note. Classifying its six documentary subjects does not establish that any processor supplies the recommended documentation.

Recommended documentation of program-size limits. Assessing actual adherence would require versioned processor documentation, applicable configurations, stated bounds and independent review; no such adherence is claimed.

Recommended documentation of program-complexity limits, distinct from size. An optional documentary assessment must retain that distinction; a benchmark or observed compilation failure is not documentation.

Recommended documentation of how exceeded limits are reported. Assessing adherence would require a versioned description of the mechanisms and invocation/configuration, independently checked against the stated limit categories.

Recommended definitions of allowed additional forms and relationships. A qualified extension inventory and its compatibility premises would support a documentary assessment; a few accepted extensions do not establish completeness.

Recommended description of means for reporting additional forms and relationships. Exact versioned reporting modes and their covered categories, not one observed warning, would establish adherence to this advice.

Recommended description of reporting deleted and obsolescent forms. Any documentary assessment must preserve both categories and the p3 exception without upgrading advice to mandatory documentation or fatal rejection.
PDF 47 lines 8-9: for this documentation discussion, use of a deleted form counts as use of an additional form. This definition remains separate from the surrounding recommendations.

PDF 47 lines 10-11 recommends documentation of processor-dependent methods or semantics. Assessing actual adherence would require version-bound processor evidence linked to the relevant facilities and choices. The should remains advisory; classification is not documentary approval or an execution result.

review_rationale: Independent original-source and corrected ledger review: doc/source_audits/execution_ledger_001.json. Universal execution, processor limits, non-Fortran portability and documentation modality remain qualified. The ledger is observational only. Current inventory adjudication includes explicitly unresolved members without approving them or completing the pending facet.
